edges.description: Losing the large beta-1 subunit disables the heterotetrameric adaptor that sorts cargo at the trans-Golgi network.
The copper-transporting ATPase ATP7A depends on AP-1 for its trafficking, and patient fibroblasts show the mislocalisation directly.
The cellular trafficking defect appears systemically as low circulating copper and ceruloplasmin.

The skin phenotype. Copper is a cofactor for enzymes of keratinisation and hair-shaft formation, which is the standard account, but no source cited here traces the route from the copper defect to the skin in this disease.
Enteropathy with feeding difficulties and failure to thrive, present in essentially every reported patient and a leading cause of early death.

The erythroderma arm of the skin phenotype, drawn separately from the ichthyosis edge because the two are listed as separate features and the HP ichthyosis binding does not cover it. Same caveat: no cited source traces the route from the copper defect.

Palmoplantar keratoderma, one of the core features in the systematic comparison across all reported individuals. As with the ichthyosis, no cited source traces the route from the copper defect to the keratinisation phenotype.

Sparse and brittle hair, a core feature. Copper is a cofactor for the cross-linking chemistry of the hair shaft, which is the usual account offered in the copper disorders, but it is not demonstrated in this disease by any source cited here.

Sensorineural deafness, a core feature and the "D" of the acronym. The route is not traced in this disease; the copper-cofactor account is inherited from the wider copper disorders rather than demonstrated here.

Global developmental delay, one of the defining features in the GeneReviews summary. Whether it is a consequence of the copper defect, of the enteropathy and malnutrition, or of a separate AP-1-dependent neuronal requirement is not established.
Keratitis, the "K" of the acronym, grouped by GeneReviews with the other ocular manifestations. Corneal epithelium is copper-dependent in the wider literature but no cited source traces that here.

Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency, reported in the severe end of the spectrum and sitting upstream of the growth failure. As with the enteropathy edge, no cited source traces the route from the copper defect to the pancreas.
Recurrent infections. Two candidate routes are open and neither is established here: the neutropenia below, and the fact that copper deficiency of any cause impairs neutrophil function.

Liver disease. This is the target most exposed to the unresolved copper-arm question: in MEDNIK the hepatic phenotype is attributed to copper overload, and the zinc therapy recommended for KIDAR is aimed at liver copper, yet the founding AP1B1 patients showed the deficiency arm rather than hepatic overload.

Anemia. Copper deficiency anemia is a well-described entity outside this disease, and the index patient's anemia was reported in the same sentence as the low serum copper, but the two are not shown to be causally linked in this disease.
Neutropenia, reported alongside the copper deficiency in the same patient.
Thrombocytopenia, reported alongside the copper deficiency in the same patient.
Cerebral atrophy on MRI in a subset. Reported as an imaging finding of the disease only; nothing cited here connects it to the copper defect specifically rather than to the AP-1 loss more broadly.
Thin corpus callosum on MRI in a subset, with the same caveat as the cerebral atrophy edge above.

Photophobia as a consequence of corneal inflammation. GeneReviews groups the two as ocular manifestations of the disease and does not order them; the direction here is the standard corneal one rather than something demonstrated in this disease.
Corneal scarring as the structural sequela of repeated or chronic keratitis, and the route by which the ocular involvement becomes vision-limiting. Same caveat on direction as the photophobia edge.

Failure to thrive as the nutritional consequence of the enteropathy and its feeding difficulties. Note the source's own "consequent" attaches to the pancreatic insufficiency rather than to the enteropathy, so that clause is not evidence for this edge as drawn; the pancreatic route is curated separately below and this edge records the broader malabsorptive one.

Intellectual disability as the persisting outcome of the early global delay. The source lists the two together as defining features and does not state that one becomes the other, so this edge records the conventional developmental ordering only.
The one downstream link in this entry that a source states rather than co-lists. The systematic review's index patient had neonatal pancreatic insufficiency "with consequent failure to thrive".
Recurrent infection progressing to sepsis, reported both as a complication in individual patients and as a cause of early death in the natural-history summary.

nodes.description: The AP-1 clathrin adaptor complex cannot perform its cargo-sorting role at the trans-Golgi network. Because the complex has several subunits and two of them now cause human disease, this node is where the AP1B1 and AP1S1 disorders converge, and it is why they share a phenotype and a treatment.

evidence.snippet: The diagnosis of IDEDNIK syndrome is established in a proband by identification of biallelic pathogenic variants in AP1B1 or AP1S1 by molecular genetic testing.

nodes.description: ATP7A is not delivered to where it must be to move copper across membranes and into the secretory pathway. The functional consequence is the same as in MEDNIK: a systemic copper-handling defect produced without any variant in a copper transporter.

evidence.reference_title: Homozygous Loss-of-Function Mutations in AP1B1, Encoding Beta-1 Subunit of Adaptor-Related Protein Complex 1, Cause MEDNIK-like Syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Functional characterization of fibroblasts derived from affected individuals closely resembles the abnormal ATP7A trafficking described in MEDNIK syndrome both at baseline and in response to copper treatment.

nodes.description: Persistent mild anemia, one of a three-lineage cytopenia picture.

evidence.reference_title: Severe KIDAR syndrome caused by deletion in the AP1B1 gene: Report of a teenage patient and systematic review of the literature.
evidence.snippet: Persistent mild anemia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, and low serum copper, ceruloplasmin and growth hormone were also present.

nodes.description: Homozygous or compound heterozygous null variants in AP1B1. The reported allelic spectrum includes nonsense and frameshift alleles and at least two whole-exon deletions, which is why copy-number analysis is recommended alongside sequencing when the diagnosis is suspected.

evidence.reference_title: Homozygous Loss-of-Function Mutations in AP1B1, Encoding Beta-1 Subunit of Adaptor-Related Protein Complex 1, Cause MEDNIK-like Syndrome.
evidence.snippet: We describe three individuals from two unrelated families in whom a MEDNIK-like phenotype segregates with two homozygous null variants in AP1B1, encoding the large beta subunit of the AP-1 complex.

evidence.reference_title: Severe KIDAR syndrome caused by deletion in the AP1B1 gene: Report of a teenage patient and systematic review of the literature.
evidence.snippet: Autosomal recessive keratitis-ichthyosis-deafness syndrome (KIDAR MIM #242150) is a very rare disorder caused by pathogenic loss-of-function variants in the AP1B1 gene.

genetic_context.description: Null alleles, including at least two multi-exon deletions. No genotype-phenotype correlation has been established, which is unsurprising at this sample size.

nodes.description: Cerebral atrophy on brain MRI, reported in a subset of individuals.

evidence.snippet: Some individuals have findings on brain MRI (cerebral atrophy, basal ganglia abnormalities, and thin corpus callosum).

evidence.reference_title: Severe KIDAR syndrome caused by deletion in the AP1B1 gene: Report of a teenage patient and systematic review of the literature.
evidence.snippet: Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed cerebral atrophy and thin corpus callosum.

nodes.description: Ichthyosis with erythroderma from birth, the presenting feature. The binding is to HP:0008064 Ichthyosis, which carries only the scaling half of the compound term, so the erythroderma is curated as its own phenotype below rather than being lost in this binding.

evidence.snippet: IDEDNIK syndrome is characterized by enteropathy, poor weight gain, growth deficiency, skin manifestations (ichthyosis, erythroderma, and keratoderma), sparse hair, global developmental delay, mild-to-severe intellectual disability, and deafness.

nodes.description: Corneal scarring, the structural sequel of the keratitis.

evidence.snippet: Additional manifestations can include liver disease, recurrent infections, and hematologic and ocular manifestations (photophobia, corneal scarring, and keratitis).

nodes.description: Developmental and educational support for the global delay and intellectual disability. GeneReviews states it as a management item without naming a modality or an intensity.

evidence.snippet: developmental and educational support; hearing aids as needed for sensorineural hearing loss; community hearing services

nodes.description: Generalised erythroderma, the second half of the "ichthyosiform erythroderma" that names the disease. Curated separately because the HP ichthyosis binding above does not carry it.

evidence.reference_title: Phenotypic spectrum of autosomal recessive Keratitis-Ichthyosis-Deafness Syndrome (KIDAR) due to mutations in AP1B1.
evidence.snippet: The main phenotypic features of KIDAR are ichthyosis, keratitis, erythroderma, and progressive hearing loss accompanied by developmental delay and failure to thrive.

IDEDNIK syndrome is characterized by enteropathy, poor weight gain, growth deficiency, skin manifestations (ichthyosis, erythroderma, and keratoderma), sparse hair, global developmental delay, mild-to-severe intellectual disability, and deafness.

nodes.description: Neonatal exocrine pancreatic insufficiency, reported in the severe end of the spectrum. Curated as its own node because it is the antecedent the source's "consequent" actually attaches to: the failure-to-thrive claim in that sentence is about the pancreatic lesion, not about the enteropathy, and collapsing the two would attribute an asserted causal order to the wrong edge.

evidence.reference_title: Severe KIDAR syndrome caused by deletion in the AP1B1 gene: Report of a teenage patient and systematic review of the literature.
evidence.snippet: The patient had fetal ascites, neonatal pancreatic insufficiency with consequent failure to thrive, feeding difficulties, recurrent infections and sepsis.

nodes.description: Poor weight gain and growth deficiency, universal in reported patients.

evidence.reference_title: Phenotypic spectrum of autosomal recessive Keratitis-Ichthyosis-Deafness Syndrome (KIDAR) due to mutations in AP1B1.
evidence.snippet: The main phenotypic features of KIDAR are ichthyosis, keratitis, erythroderma, and progressive hearing loss accompanied by developmental delay and failure to thrive.

nodes.description: Gastrostomy as needed, for the subset in whom feeding therapy is not sufficient. The "as needed" is the source's own hedge and is kept.

evidence.snippet: gastrostomy tube placement as needed

nodes.description: Developmental delay with mild-to-severe intellectual disability.

evidence.snippet: IDEDNIK syndrome is characterized by enteropathy, poor weight gain, growth deficiency, skin manifestations (ichthyosis, erythroderma, and keratoderma), sparse hair, global developmental delay, mild-to-severe intellectual disability, and deafness.

nodes.description: Amplification as needed for the sensorineural hearing loss, with community hearing services. The NCIT hearing-aid term names the device and is not reachable from Clinical Intervention or Procedure, so the action is bound to Rehabilitation and the device is carried as a qualifier.
nodes.id: Hearing Aids and Community Hearing Services

evidence.snippet: developmental and educational support; hearing aids as needed for sensorineural hearing loss; community hearing services

nodes.description: Intellectual disability spanning mild to severe, distinct from and outlasting the early global developmental delay.

evidence.snippet: IDEDNIK syndrome is characterized by enteropathy, poor weight gain, growth deficiency, skin manifestations (ichthyosis, erythroderma, and keratoderma), sparse hair, global developmental delay, mild-to-severe intellectual disability, and deafness.

nodes.description: Corneal inflammation, part of the ocular triad with photophobia and scarring.

evidence.snippet: Additional manifestations can include liver disease, recurrent infections, and hematologic and ocular manifestations (photophobia, corneal scarring, and keratitis).

nodes.description: Liver involvement is a recognised additional manifestation. Note that the KIDAR literature does not resolve whether this reflects hepatic copper accumulation as in MEDNIK; see the copper-arm knowledge gap.

evidence.snippet: Additional manifestations can include liver disease, recurrent infections, and hematologic and ocular manifestations (photophobia, corneal scarring, and keratitis).

nodes.description: Neutropenia, part of the same cytopenia picture and plausibly relevant to the infection burden.

evidence.reference_title: Severe KIDAR syndrome caused by deletion in the AP1B1 gene: Report of a teenage patient and systematic review of the literature.
evidence.snippet: Persistent mild anemia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, and low serum copper, ceruloplasmin and growth hormone were also present.

nodes.description: Dietary modification with parenteral supplementation where the enteral route is insufficient, plus feeding therapy. This is supportive care for the enteropathy, not a treatment of the underlying trafficking defect, and GeneReviews states it as management practice rather than as a studied intervention.

evidence.snippet: Supportive care: Dietary modification and potential parenteral supplementation for enteropathy; feeding therapy; gastrostomy tube placement as needed

nodes.description: Targeted therapy aimed at reducing liver copper overload, reported to improve behavioural disturbance, skin manifestations and cognitive function in some individuals. It is the only mechanism-directed treatment described for this disorder, and it is important not to overstate it: GeneReviews says experience is limited, the benefit is reported in some patients rather than demonstrated in a trial, and its rationale involves liver copper overload, which the founding AP1B1 report specifically did not find in its patients.

evidence.snippet: Treatment with oral zinc acetate therapy to reduce liver copper overload has been reported to improve behavioral disturbances, skin manifestations, and cognitive function in some individuals.
Experience is limited with this targeted therapy.

nodes.description: Conspicuous thickening of palmar and plantar skin.

evidence.reference_title: Severe KIDAR syndrome caused by deletion in the AP1B1 gene: Report of a teenage patient and systematic review of the literature.
evidence.snippet: Comparing the phenotypes of all reported individuals, they are highly concordant and major features are enteropathy with feeding difficulties, failure to thrive, ichthyosis, palmoplantar keratoderma, sensorineural deafness and sparse and brittle hair.

nodes.description: Light sensitivity, reported with the corneal involvement.

evidence.snippet: Additional manifestations can include liver disease, recurrent infections, and hematologic and ocular manifestations (photophobia, corneal scarring, and keratitis).

nodes.description: Clarifying the genotype of apparently asymptomatic sibs so that zinc acetate can be started early. This is recorded as a treatment rather than only as a diagnostic action because its stated purpose is to bring forward the one mechanism-directed therapy the disorder has, which makes it a timing intervention on that therapy.
nodes.id: Presymptomatic Genetic Evaluation of At-Risk Sibs

evidence.snippet: Evaluation of relatives at risk: Clarify the genetic status of apparently asymptomatic older and younger at-risk sibs in order to identify as early as possible those who would benefit from prompt initiation of zinc acetate treatment.

nodes.description: Recurrent infections are a recognised additional manifestation and, in the severe end of the spectrum, progress to sepsis.

evidence.snippet: Additional manifestations can include liver disease, recurrent infections, and hematologic and ocular manifestations (photophobia, corneal scarring, and keratitis).

nodes.description: Congenital-onset, often profound, bilateral sensorineural deafness. The phenotype term carries clinical_course PROGRESSIVE because the KIDAR phenotypic-spectrum review describes the hearing loss as progressive; congenital onset and a progressive course are both reported and are not in conflict.

nodes.description: Sepsis complicating recurrent infection, and a reported cause of early death.

nodes.description: Enteropathy with feeding difficulties, and one of the two named causes of death before age two.

evidence.snippet: Death prior to age two years occurs in some individuals due to severe enteropathy or sepsis; in others survival into adulthood is reported.

nodes.description: Sparse and brittle hair, a core feature.

evidence.snippet: standard treatment for recurrent infections

nodes.description: Supportive management of the cytopenias, with transfusion where necessary. The "occasionally" is the source's own frequency qualifier for transfusion and is kept.

evidence.snippet: supportive treatment as needed for hematologic manifestations, and occasionally transfusion may be necessary

nodes.description: Low serum copper and low ceruloplasmin. Note the asymmetry with MEDNIK: the copper deficiency arm is present and the hepatic copper toxicity arm was not demonstrated in the founding AP1B1 patients, although later guidance describes zinc therapy aimed at liver copper overload. This entry does not resolve that tension and marks it as a knowledge gap.

evidence.snippet: Reduced serum ceruloplasmin and total copper levels are common.

evidence.reference_title: Homozygous Loss-of-Function Mutations in AP1B1, Encoding Beta-1 Subunit of Adaptor-Related Protein Complex 1, Cause MEDNIK-like Syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Taken together, our results expand the list of inborn errors of copper metabolism.

nodes.description: Thin corpus callosum on brain MRI, reported alongside the cerebral atrophy.

evidence.snippet: Some individuals have findings on brain MRI (cerebral atrophy, basal ganglia abnormalities, and thin corpus callosum).

evidence.snippet: Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed cerebral atrophy and thin corpus callosum.

nodes.description: Thrombocytopenia, the third lineage of the reported cytopenia.

nodes.description: Emollients, topical lactic acid, 50% urea ointments, and short courses of topical corticosteroid or pimecrolimus. This is the non-systemic arm of skin management, sitting alongside the low-dose oral acitretin recorded separately above.

evidence.snippet: treatment options for skin manifestations include low-dose oral acitretin, skin emollients and topical lactic acid, frequent emollient application and short courses of topical cortical steroids or pimecrolimus ointment, and 50% urea ointments
